P0234.note: The campus is the first CloudBurst Data Centers gigacenter, planned between San Marcos and New Braunfels in Central Texas. CloudBurst is a Denver firm founded in 2022. A Community Impact report from May 2025 puts the site on a 96-acre parcel off Francis Harris Lane that straddles Hays County and Guadalupe County. The full campus is planned at 1.2 GW, with a first 50 MW phase due online in the fourth quarter of 2026. A w.media article from November 2025 says a groundbreaking was held and that no tenant is named. Power would come from a behind-the-meter natural gas plant on site. Energy Transfer agreed to supply up to 450,000 million British thermal units per day for 10 years, and w.media says delivery is through the Oasis Pipeline. Community Impact and Data Center Dynamics say only that the gas comes through a pipeline running through the site. CloudBurst also plans a separate 200 MW site in Oklahoma.

P7810.note: No single data center is named for this project. A Boardwalk press release from December 2024 says the pipeline supplies gas needed to support the growth of data centers and industrial demand, and ties it to electric generation demand in Mississippi and the Southeast. The pipeline is backed by one unnamed anchor customer on a 20-year agreement, and Boardwalk is still negotiating the rest of the capacity. A Hart Energy article from December 2024 repeats that Boardwalk called it a response to growing data center and power generation demand in the Southeast, especially Mississippi. Target in-service is the first half of 2029. No source read ties the pipeline to a specific campus, developer, tenant or power plant.

P8234.note: The campus is the Monarch Compute Campus, an artificial intelligence data center in Mason County, West Virginia, near Point Pleasant. A March 2026 press release from American Intelligence and Power Corporation names it as developer and calls the Hope Gas Prosperity Line a component of the campus. Nscale and Fidelis Energy are now named as developers on the Nscale web page and in a WSAZ report from April 2026. Nscale says phase 1 is 1.35 GW of compute with delivery targeted for early 2028 and room to grow to more than 8 GW, on more than 2,250 acres, with more than $20 billion of investment. WSAZ reports a $40 billion figure and operations in the second half of 2027. A Marcellus Drilling News article from March 2026 says an initial 2 GW of power generation would be supported by the pipeline. Nscale says the campus makes all its own power on site with Caterpillar equipment and is independent of the public grid. No tenant is named.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The pipeline feeds the Socrates South power plant in New Albany, Licking County, Ohio. The plant is 200 MW and burns natural gas. A Pipeline and Gas Journal report from June 2025 says the Ohio Power Siting Board approved it, that Williams builds and operates it, and that a Meta affiliate, Sidecat LLC, will use the power. The plant is behind the meter and is not connected to the electric grid, and its gas is to come from two 24-inch pipelines to be filed separately. A page from Williams lists Socrates North and Socrates South as two 200 MW plants on about 20 acres each, with in-service targets in the third and fourth quarters of 2026. A mgrid.org article from June 2025 says the plants serve a Meta campus in New Albany tied to its Prometheus supercluster and puts total investment above $2 billion. That article also lists 400 MW across both sites and a campus of 740 acres, which the Williams page and the regulator report do not confirm. No source read states outright that this pipeline serves the campus, so the link runs through the plant.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The campus is Meta's Hyperion data center in Richland Parish, Louisiana, described by E&E News in March 2026 as Meta's largest planned data center. Entergy Louisiana is building gas plants to power it. A Gas Processing article from August 2025 says state regulators approved three plants totaling about 2.3 GW. Two are in Richland Parish and due online in late 2028, and the third is at the Waterford site in St. Charles Parish, due by the end of 2029. E&E News reports that in March 2026 Meta agreed to fund seven more plants, for 10 in total and 5.2 GW of new gas power, and calls the data center still planned. A Pipeline and Gas Journal report from November 2025 says Energy Transfer and Entergy Louisiana signed a 20-year deal for 250,000 million British thermal units per day of firm gas transport, running from February 2028 through January 2048. The gas serves Entergy's planned plants and Meta's data center.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The campus is Meta's data center in northeast El Paso, Texas, built on about 1,000 acres. A Texas Tribune article from January 2026 gives 1 GW and $1.5 billion, with groundbreaking in October 2025. An analyst post from Measured AI in 2026 gives 960 MW of computing load on 1,039 acres, about 4 million square feet, and a cost of $14.3 billion. It says a BlackRock-led venture owns 80 percent and Meta 20 percent, with Meta as tenant, and that the project was code-named Project Seafox. Power comes from the McCloud plant, a 366 MW natural gas plant that El Paso Electric would own. Measured AI says Enchanted Rock builds it and that it would run alone at 225 MW by mid-2027. Its state approval is contested, with a regulatory deadline of December 9, 2026. The same post says the gas comes from El Paso Natural Gas through a McCloud Lateral with 167,000 dekatherms per day from January 1, 2027. Measured AI says rent starts December 1, 2028. No regulator or company document read names the lateral and the campus together.
